originalSourceOnlyContract.exact_statement_normalized: Let alpha in (0,1), phi:(0,1)->(0,1-ln 2) defined as phi(alpha):=1/(2-alpha)+((1/2)^(1-alpha)-1)/(1-alpha), and T>=2/((1-alpha)phi(alpha)). For unprojected OSD with stepsizes eta_t=t^(-alpha) and x_1=0, there exists a sequence of T convex and 1-Lipschitz losses such that Regret_T(0)>=(1/2)phi(alpha)T^(2-alpha). Also, lim_{alpha->1}phi(alpha)=1-ln 2>=0.3.

quantifier_contract.dimension: Every positive integer d, implicit in proof cases d=1 and d>=2.
quantifier_contract.horizon: For each integer T satisfying T>=2/((1-alpha)*phi(alpha)); source infers T>=2.
quantifier_contract.losses: There exists a sequence (ell_1,...,ell_T) of convex 1-Lipschitz functions R^d->R. Witness depends on T through ceil/floor split.
quantifier_contract.algorithm: Run unprojected OSD from zero with eta_t=t^(-alpha), t=1,...,T.
quantifier_contract.comparator: Only u=0 in the lower-bound conclusion.
quantifier_contract.horizon_not_interchangeable: For each T there is a length-T witness. Source does not produce one infinite sequence simultaneously witnessing every horizon.
quantifier_contract.rate: For fixed alpha in (0,1), exponent 2-alpha in (1,2), positive alpha-dependent coefficient. Not an alpha-uniform constant 0.3.
quantifier_contract.dimension_dependence: No d factor; first-coordinate embedding preserves regret and Euclidean Lipschitz constant.

input_classification.input: T is integer, rounds indexed 1..T, predictions through x_{T+1}
positive dimension d and Euclidean space R^d
OSD update and comparator regret convention

input_classification.note: Not arbitrary externally given losses and not a new premise supplying the lower bound.

witness.adversary: Deterministic, fixed before play, horizon-dependent. No stochastic/expectation/high-probability claim.
witness.subgradient: Unique slopes -1,+1 in d=1, or -e_1,+e_1 in positive dimension.
witness.iterate_boundary: Both expressions agree at t=m+1. The update at round T defines x_{T+1}, but regret sums x_1,...,x_T.

probability_and_feedback.feedback: Subgradient available after each output/loss, as Algorithm 2.2. Not bandit-only scalar-loss feedback.
